geometry_edits.rationale: Change the dominant mass from generic setback stacking to a terrace-based section that can read as one continuous inhabited rule.
Keep the terracing organized along the long dimension so the mass remains a bar rather than a tower-like stack.
Maintain limited hierarchy while avoiding excessive tier repetition.
Reduce the stepped pyramid impression and keep the upper mass calm.
Turn the cave into a clearer public court to establish a ground-level social void.
Make the courtyard large enough to register in all views.
Open the court to the access side so the frontage becomes legible and public.

graph_edits.rationale: Replace the generic setback layering with a more programmatic terrace linkage to turn the stepped mass into one continuous inhabited section rather than a pyramidal stack.
Keep the hierarchy compact while reducing the impression of repetitive code-like stepbacks.
Soften the pyramid effect and preserve a calmer upper mass.
Convert the shallow cave into a proper public void/courtyard to strengthen the ground threshold and give the access edge a legible spatial response.
Increase the void’s readability so it becomes a usable public court rather than a minor subtraction.
Align the public void to the verified access side to reinforce the active frontage relation.

rationale: The candidate reads coherently in the four views as a single stepped mass, so it has a clear dominant gesture and acceptable repair integrity. However, the form is still primarily an abstract terraced block rather than a neighborhood-living building with an active street threshold and a meaningful public ground. The blue access edge is acknowledged only weakly: there is no clear carved entry court, undercut, or seam aligned to that frontage, and the visible voids are shallow/not sufficiently public. The section is also too pyramid-like and stair-stepped relative to the program brief; it feels more like stacked setbacks than a capacity-aware mixed-use bar with one legible public void and calm upper massing. The mass does not visibly develop a strong neighborhood public-space figure or a convincing active-ground relation, so program_fit_hard_pass fails.
